skill.name: analyzing-component-quality
skill.description: Expert at analyzing the quality and effectiveness of Claude Code components (agents, skills, commands, hooks). Assumes component is already technically valid. Evaluates description clarity, tool permissions, auto-invoke triggers, security, and usability to provide quality scores and improvement suggestions.
skill.summary: Analyzes Claude Code components for clarity, permissions, triggers, security, and usability.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection or malicious data-exfiltration intent was found. The static backtick and reconnaissance hits are Markdown examples or checklist text, but Bash access needs clear execution guardrails.

remediation.suggestion: Remove Bash if manual review is enough, or restrict use to trusted local helper scripts with validated paths.

remediation.issue: Helper command guidance lacks path safety rules
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to pass only local component files and avoid shell-expanded, remote, or untrusted paths.

remediation.issue: Documentation references helper scripts that are not included
remediation.suggestion: Remove missing script references or include tested scripts before marketplace publication.

static_findings.snippet: **4.0 - Good**: Solid component, some enhancements recommended
- `Bash, Write, Edit` - Command injection + file access
- Does it have appropriate `{baseDir}` usage for resources?
**Current**: `allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob, WebSearch, WebFetch, Task`
**Current**: `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, WebSearch, WebFetch, Task`
- **Quality ≠ Correctness**: Valid components can still be low quality

semantic_findings.title: Broad Bash Permission for Review Workflow
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md grants Bash and instructs reviewers to run local helper scripts against component paths. This is not malicious, but it expands execution authority for a review-focused skill.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The frontmatter grants Bash and the documentation recommends local Python helper commands. No exfiltration or shell interpolation was found, so the risk is permission breadth.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent reviews before they publish Claude Code components. This skill scores clarity, permissions, triggers, security, and usability with concrete improvement guidance.
actual_capabilities: Scores descriptions, tool permissions, triggers, security, and usability on a 1-5 scale.
Reviews agents, skills, commands, and hooks using documented quality standards.
Uses a local quality scorer script for heuristic checks when Bash is available.
Produces issue lists with priority, rationale, impact, and suggested rewrites.
Checks marketplace readiness against minimum quality and documentation standards.
Identifies unsafe tool combinations and missing input validation guidance.
limitations: Assumes the component already passed technical validation.
Automated scoring is heuristic and still needs reviewer judgment.
Referenced effectiveness and optimization helper scripts are not included.
Bash permission should be constrained to trusted local helper scripts.

use_cases.title: Review a New Skill
use_cases.description: Score a draft skill before publishing and get specific fixes for weak triggers, permissions, or documentation.

use_cases.title: Standardize Marketplace Audits
use_cases.description: Apply the same quality rubric across submitted agents, skills, commands, and hooks.

use_cases.title: Improve Internal Automation
use_cases.description: Find unclear invocation rules and excessive tools in internal Claude Code components.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Claude Code component for quality. Score each dimension and list the top three improvements: [path or pasted content].

prompt_templates.title: Check Marketplace Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component against marketplace standards. Identify blockers, important fixes, and a concise revised description: [component].

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these two Claude Code components across clarity, tools, triggers, security, and usability. Recommend the stronger option: [components].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Review Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a repeatable review workflow for our Claude Code components. Include scoring rules, reviewer checks, and remediation priorities: [context].

output_examples.input: A skill description is vague and lists Bash, Write, and Edit.
output: Overall quality is poor because the purpose and trigger are unclear.
Tool permissions are excessive for an analysis skill.
Recommended action is to narrow tools and rewrite the description with specific triggers.

output_examples.input: An agent has clear docs but includes Task without an orchestration role.
output: Quality is adequate, but tool permissions need review.
The report recommends removing Task or explaining why delegation is required.
The highest impact change is clarifying when the agent should be invoked.

output_examples.input: A command has useful arguments but no examples or success criteria.
output: Add realistic usage examples and describe the expected result.
The command can pass after documentation and trigger clarity improve.

best_practices: Provide the component file and explain its intended users.
Ask for evidence-based scores and exact lines that need changes.
Review security findings before accepting style recommendations.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a pass or fail without requesting improvement guidance.
Do not treat heuristic scores as a complete security review.
Do not run helper scripts on untrusted paths without checking inputs.

faq.question: Can this skill validate component syntax?
faq.answer: No. It assumes technical validation is already complete and focuses on quality, usability, and security review.

faq.question: Which component types does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Claude Code agents, skills, commands, and hooks.

faq.question: Does it run code during review?
faq.answer: It can use a local quality scorer script when Bash is available. Reviewers should run only trusted local scripts.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. Marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What does the output include?
faq.answer: It includes scores, issue priorities, evidence, suggested rewrites, and marketplace readiness guidance.

faq.question: Is this a full security scanner?
faq.answer: No. It highlights design risks and unsafe permissions, but it does not replace dedicated security testing.
